title: Investigation on mechanical properties and creep behavior of stir cast AZ91-SiCp composites

nodes.label: AZ91 castings lose strength and creep resistance above 150 C, which keeps Mg out of hot powertrain parts
Adding SiC particles should raise the strength and the creep resistance of the AZ91 matrix
AZ91 as the matrix alloy
Add SiC particles as the reinforcing phase
SiCp content 0-25 wt% in 5 wt% steps, with creep at 175 C under 80, 100 and 120 MPa
Stir casting: preheated SiCp stirred into the melt at 750 C under argon, then poured into a 300 C steel mould
SiCp are spread through the matrix, with clustering and banding that grow with loading
Matrix grain size falls from 65 um to 34 um at 5 wt% and 22 um at 10 wt%, and barely changes above that
The Mg/SiCp interface is clean and free of reaction products, with the particles well bonded to the matrix
Tensile yield strength rises monotonically from 93 MPa to 143 MPa over 0-25 wt% SiCp
Ultimate compressive strength rises monotonically from about 310 MPa to 363 MPa
Ultimate tensile strength does not benefit: it drifts down from about 188 MPa to 174 MPa
Tensile fracture is mixed ductile-brittle, the brittle share growing with SiCp content
SiCp nucleate and pin the solidifying grains, then block dislocation motion and take up load through the clean interface

attrs.mechanism_class: grain refinement, Orowan blocking and load transfer

nodes.label: The minimum creep rate at 175 C falls by about half an order of magnitude for 15-25 wt% SiCp, while 0-10 wt% barely differ
Apparent stress exponents run 7.2-8.9, and after subtracting a threshold stress the true exponents fall to 5.4-5.8
A true exponent near 5 identifies lattice-diffusion-controlled dislocation climb as the rate-controlling step, the threshold stress coming from Orowan looping around the particles

attrs.mechanism_class: climb-controlled creep with a threshold stress

nodes.label: Composites with 15 wt% SiCp and above resist creep at 175 C under 80-120 MPa
Stir-cast AZ91-SiCp gains yield and compressive strength and creep resistance through grain refinement, dislocation blocking and a particle threshold stress
Up to 10 wt% buys the grain refinement and most of the yield gain; the creep benefit needs 15 wt% or more, at the cost of tensile strength
The optical panels resolve matrix grain boundaries only in the unreinforced alloy, so the quoted refinement cannot be read from them
Above 15 wt% the particles gather into visible bands and clusters, against the reported near-uniform distribution with very few agglomerations
The interface and fracture-mode readings come from x1500 and x150 micrographs, at which neither a sub-micron reaction layer nor dimples can be resolved
The apparent exponents are not monotonic in SiCp content and each rests on a three-point fit
Dark SiCp fill the field ever more densely from 5 to 25 wt%, and from 15 wt% upward they gather into bands and clusters separated by particle-free matrix

nodes.label: SiC has a compressive strength of 3900 MPa against 310 MPa for the base alloy
SiC wets Mg well and the Al in AZ91 further improves the wettability of SiCp
A true stress exponent near 5 indicates dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion
Li and Langdon's threshold-stress method: extrapolate each creep curve to 1e-10 /s to read the threshold stress, then replot against the effective stress
The strengthening mechanisms in Mg matrix composites are particle strengthening, work hardening, load transfer and matrix grain refinement

notes: Two-branch spine from one structure state: a room-temperature branch (t10/t11/t12/t13) and a creep branch (t15 -> t16 -> t17 -> t18), meeting at the conclusion. The diagnostic chain is complete: PRP/diagnostic t16 -> KNW/lookup v3 -> MEC/identification t17, with the effective-stress replot read by collapse_by_normalization because the merge of the six lines is what carries the argument. Numbers come from the panels: YS 93-143 MPa and UTS 188-174 MPa from F3, UCS 310-363 MPa from F4, creep rates and both exponent sets from the legends of F7a and F7b. Four audits. t21 with OBS u2: only the unreinforced optical panel resolves matrix grain boundaries, so the quoted 65 -> 22 um refinement is not readable from that figure (u12 carries the numbers as text_only). t22 with OBS u1: from 15 wt% up the particles gather into bands and particle-free regions, against the reported near-uniform distribution with very few agglomerations. t23 with OBS u4 and u7: the clean-interface reading comes from an x1500 view with a 10 um bar, too coarse for a sub-micron reaction layer, and the ductile/brittle classification from x150 views in which dimples cannot be resolved. t24 with OBS u11: the apparent exponents are not monotonic (8.5 at 15 wt% against 8.4 at 20 wt%) and each rests on a three-point fit. t12 is kept on the spine as a negative result with a qualifies edge to the conclusion: the tensile strength falls with SiCp, so the packet's 'enhanced room temperature mechanical properties' holds only for yield and compressive strength. Panel-section defects: Figure 6 is tier C3_caption_swap with no panels offered, Figure 1 is tier B1_caption_empty and its b and c definitions are empty strings, and the OCR cue lines render the SEM banner bars as '108Mm', '10Mm' and '100Mm'. Lost: the XRD phase identification, the creep curves of F6, Table 1 with the threshold stresses, and the Mg17Al12 / MgO / Mg2Si phase discussion.

changes: u2: image_support lowered from shown to partial, the label softened from 'no resolved grain boundaries' to 'boundaries too faint to follow', and the image_note extended. F1c does keep faint discontinuous bright lines between the dark particles; they are too indistinct to size grains, which is what the t21 audit needs, but 'no boundaries at all' overstated the panel.
u5: image_note corrected, the F3 ordinate runs 80-220 MPa, not 100-220.

panel_checks.note: Both crops opened at their 200 um bars. F1a resolves the light matrix with its dark boundary network cleanly; F1c is dominated by dark particle contrast with only faint bright lines. The cited panels are right and the audit holds; only the strength of the statement was adjusted.

F3 opened: YS bars 93, 113, 124, 127, 136, 143 MPa and UTS bars 188, ~183, ~183, 182, 181, 174 MPa across 0-25 wt%, as the node states. The UTS decline exceeds the error bars only at 25 wt%, which the note already says.

F7b prints n_t = 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.8, 5.6, 5.7 in its legend and the six lines very nearly merge on the effective-stress abscissa. collapse_by_normalization is the right op: the merge is what carries the argument, and the threshold stresses that set the abscissa are tabulated, not plotted, as the note says.

review.audit_summary: Six audit nodes by the derived-ring count (t21-t24 plus the OBS u2 and u11), one over the soft budget, but none is redundant: t21 with u2 bounds the grain-size claim t8, t22 bounds the distribution claim t7, t23 bounds both the clean-interface claim t9 and the fracture-mode claim t13 by naming the x1500 and x150 magnifications, and t24 with u11 bounds the diagnostic t16 (non-monotonic apparent exponents from three-point fits). u2's support was downgraded after the judge's own read. The diagnostic chain required by v04 is complete and correctly typed: PRP/diagnostic t16 -> KNW/lookup v3 -> MEC/identification t17. u9, u10 and u11 are derived OBS with derives edges from u8, and u12 is a text-only OBS with no figs and no mm_op. No invented panel ids; packet F6 is tier C (caption swap) and is not cited.
